mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport bio-data page for each individual UBO, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of each individual's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for conventional countries; otherwise consular legalization through the competent Canadian diplomatic or consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified copy of proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill issued within the last 3 months) with certified translation if not in English or French
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or utility provider in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent registry extract for any corporate UBO holding 25% or more of the ULC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar of the foreign jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for conventional countries; consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions; certified English or French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed declaration of source of wealth and source of funds, together with bank reference letter or broker statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Beneficial owner or the financial institution providing the reference
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarially certified signature; apostille or consular legalization if executed outside Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, signatories, and underlying beneficiaries against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, Canadian Sanctions Regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions, and UK Consolidated Sanctions List; enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification and ongoing sanctions monitoring.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_note: The BC transparency register and corporate records are accessible to government enforcement, tax, and financial intelligence authorities; they are not publicly searchable as a standalone open register.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online — British Columbia Registrar of Companies (Corporate Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be represented in Roman letters and may include French accent marks; no translation into a local script is required because BC corporate records are maintained in English and French. The name must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to any existing company, extra-provincial registration, society, or reserved name. A BC unlimited liability company must include the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or the abbreviation 'ULC' or 'U.L.C.'. Numbers may be written as numerals or words; punctuation and corporate connectors are standardized for search purposes; names must not contain misleading or restricted language.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant may request written reasons from the BC Registrar. The applicant may modify the name or distinctiveness argument and resubmit a new name reservation request. Reconsideration may be sought from the Assistant Registrar of Companies under the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57. If administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, judicial review may be filed in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. The 56-day reservation window cannot be extended, but a new reservation may be filed without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only if the virtual office maintains a physical street address in British Columbia, is not a P.O. Box, accepts service of process, and has facilities capable of receiving and forwarding corporate records. The registered office must satisfy section 36 of the Business Corporations Act and be accessible for inspection. For a web novel subscription and reading platform, no industry-specific physical location is required; however, tax and bank KYC considerations favor a BC street address, local representation, and demonstrable records-keeping substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-negligible: approximately 3-8% annual likelihood of a registry records inspection or demand for production in the first year for a standard low-risk digital services company; the likelihood is materially higher if foreign control is present or if the registrar receives information suggesting the registered office is ineffective. The registrar may require production of records under section 226 of the Business Corporations Act.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, Part 2 (Incorporation), ss. 10-24, and Part 2.1; applicable provisions governing the designation of an Unlimited Liability Company
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, and Articles filed through BC Registries Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; shares may be issued for any lawful consideration as determined by the board of directors
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company subscribe for the initial common shares listed in Schedule A and that the board issue those shares in accordance with the Business Corporations Act for the consideration approved by the directors. RESOLVED, that the registered office and records office shall be located at the address stated in the Notice of Articles and shall remain at that address until changed by valid resolution. RESOLVED, that [President], [Secretary], and [Treasurer] be appointed as officers. RESOLVED, that all acts of the incorporators be ratified and that officers are authorized to execute all filings, contracts, and banking documents necessary to complete incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Corporate Online - Name Request Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request through the BC Registries online portal using the proposed corporate name, including the mandatory ULC or Unlimited Liability Company designator. Pay the name reservation fee electronically and await the automatic NUANS-style search result before filing incorporation documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as confusingly similar, file an amended name request with a more distinctive element or provide a written consent from the holder of the conflicting name and resubmit through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal Counsel or Authorized BC Corporate Services Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles and Notice of Articles for a BC Unlimited Liability Company. Set the unlimited liability of shareholders, share structure, registered office address, records office address, first directors, and permitted business purposes. Verify that the constitutional documents comply with the Business Corporations Act and are ready for execution by the incorporators.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office address details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a deficiency in the draft, correct the identified schedule, restate the affected provision, and file an amended Incorporation Application or a corrective filing with BC Registries Corporate Online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries e-Signing Module / Authorized Notary or Lawyer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain duly executed signatures from each incorporator and first director. The Incorporation Application, Articles, and consent to act as director forms may be executed using the secure BC Registries online account or by paper counterpart signatures verified by legal counsel. No notarization is mandatory for domestic BC filings unless the registry requires identity verification.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act as director forms
Incorporator identification and professional endorsement, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If consent forms are rejected for incomplete execution, obtain fresh signatures and upload scanned executed copies; where the registry requires proof of identity, provide certified true copies of officer identification with the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the BC Registries Corporate Online system, enter the company's required corporate data, upload the executed constitutional documents, select the ULC entity type, pay the applicable filing fee using an approved card or BC Registries account, and submit the incorporation transaction. Standard or expedited processing may be selected.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected or queried, review the registrar's deficiency notice, correct the data entry or document conclusion within the stated response period, pay any refiling fee, and resubmit through Corporate Online; expedited processing is available for urgent corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate and Establishment of Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Certificate of Incorporation and date-stamped Notice of Articles from Corporate Online. Establish the corporate minute book at the records office and prepare the registers of directors, members, and allotments. Maintain statutory records as required by the Business Corporations Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the original certificate is not issued, request a certified copy through the BC Registries document ordering service; if the registered office is unable to receive service, change the registered office by filing a Notice of Change of Registered Office with BC Registries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Officers and Federal/Provincial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; BC Registries
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause the first board of directors to pass a written resolution appointing the initial officers. Thereafter register the company for a CRA Business Number and GST/HST account using Business Registration Online. File any required BC provincial corporate information via BC Registries, including officer changes, and record the officers in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: BC Registries officer update or Notice of Articles amendment, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or BC Registries queries the filing, provide the Certificate of Incorporation, corporate legal name, registered office address, and director/officer identification; correct any conflicting data and resubmit the account registration or information update.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 9000 serialized digital web fiction is a non-industrial online publishing activity; no physical manufacturing establishment is established in British Columbia under this scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating licence or manufacturing permit required for the web novel subscription app business model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Government of British Columbia
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity is a digital content service with no reviewable project threshold under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2018, c. 41; no environmental assessment application is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for direct pollutant discharge. General office operations, if any, shall comply with municipal sewer and solid waste bylaws and the provincial Environmental Management Act for any negligible electronic waste disposal; regulated wastewater and VOC discharge thresholds are not triggered by the absence of physical processing facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certification, structural load inspection, or workplace clearance applies while the business operates exclusively from digital infrastructure. If a physical office or call-centre is opened in BC, a building occupancy permit and WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety compliance clearance will be required prior to employee on-site use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; Business Registration Online via canada.ca and My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A British Columbia Unlimited Liability Company is constituted under the BC Business Corporations Act and receives a provincial incorporation number. To obtain the federal Business Number (BN) and tax program accounts, the ULC must register with CRA using Business Registration Online or Form RC1, submitting the BC incorporation certificate, registered office address, expected revenue data, and director/shareholder particulars. An RT program account must be requested for GST/HST. In British Columbia, the BC Ministry of Finance Consumer Taxation Branch separately issues a PST registration number for retail sales taxable in BC. Non-resident shareholders are permitted, and a Canadian registered office or authorized representative must be designated for service of documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: CRA treats a BC ULC as a taxable corporation, and no Canadian check-the-box election is available. For U.S. federal income tax only, the ULC is an eligible entity that may file IRS Form 8832 to elect disregarded entity or partnership status; Canada's hybrid mismatch rules in Income Tax Act sections 93.1 and 94 may limit treaty or deduction benefits in such structures. Under the Excise Tax Act, registered closely-related corporations may also elect under section 156 to treat certain taxable supplies as made for nil consideration for GST/HST purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (federal goods and services tax) and BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) in parallel; BC applies no harmonized sales tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold under GST/HST, calculated on taxable supplies made over the preceding four calendar quarters; BC PST requires separate vendor registration for taxable retail sales in British Columbia and is not governed by a federal-equivalent small-supplier threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping. E-invoicing is voluntary through the Pan-Canadian Peppol network and becomes mandatory only for vendors supplying by electronic means to the federal government. CRA requires invoices and supporting records to contain prescribed information under the Excise Tax Act but does not operate an immediate fiscal approval server.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Digital subscription services and web-novel content supplied by a Canadian-registered ULC are zero-rated under GST/HST when the recipient is a non-resident who is outside Canada, the supply is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, and the intangible personal property is not for use in Canada. The supplier must obtain and retain documentary evidence of the recipient's residence and of offshore delivery/access, including payment-card origin, billing address, IP address, geolocation logs, subscription contract, and platform usage records. Tangible goods exports are zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V of the Excise Tax Act when substantiated by customary customs documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for physical goods; for digital web-novel subscriptions, replaced by CRA-acceptable digital export records and subscriber geolocation logs)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (for goods; for online platforms, use CDN access logs, IP-resolution evidence, and API delivery logs)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice evidencing foreign-currency receipt and applicable FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without sufficient substantiation, CRA may reassess the supply as taxable within the normal four-year period (or beyond where misrepresentation is shown), collect uncollected GST plus interest, deny input tax credits, and impose penalties. The Excise Tax Act authorizes a $100 plus 50% legal-confidence penalty where a false statement is made knowingly or in circumstances of gross negligence; the Customs Act separately permits monetary penalties and forfeiture for export misdeclarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central monetary authority; FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) administers AML/ATF and cross-border transaction reporting; the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) administers currency reporting for tax and customs purposes. Canada has no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration body; exchange policy is legislated under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. There are no general exchange controls, approval mechanisms, or restrictions on the repatriation of dividends, interest, royalties, or capital. A BC ULC may freely remit profits to non-resident shareholders after application of the relevant non-resident withholding tax (Part XIII), which may be reduced under treaty. Capital contributions and equity injections are unrestricted, provided they do not violate sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act or the United Nations Act. Beneficial ownership reporting to CRA and FINTRAC is required for transactions above prescribed thresholds (CAD 10,000).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds is required. Revenue from digital webnovel subscriptions and app-store sales may be retained in foreign currency. However, receipt of funds exceeding CAD 10,000 or equivalent must be reported to FINTRAC as a large cash transaction or electronic funds transfer if initiated cross-border. For Canadian income tax, all revenue must be converted to CAD at the CRA's published exchange rate for the relevant taxation year; no timeline-based conversion obligation is imposed by law.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low–Medium. Canada does not issue digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licences comparable to the EEA; foreign EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise, N26) cannot hold Canadian deposit accounts or provide Canadian routing/accounts unless registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC. A cross-border EMI may be used as a supplementary disbursement tool for author payouts under an MSB arrangement, but the ULC must maintain its primary operational and capital accounts with a Canadian chartered Tier 1 bank for CAD clearing, FX, and regulatory compliance. The payment rails from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are typically acquired through Canadian PSPs that are also FINTRAC-registered MSBs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a BC Unlimited Liability Company, under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), s. 124, at least one director must be a Canadian resident (unless the company is a public company and has obtained an exemption). This resident director is normally required for identity verification. For a low-risk domestic digital content business, most Tier 1 banks allow fully remote onboarding via video KYC and electronic signature, provided the resident director can produce Canadian government-issued ID and a copy of the company's Notice of Articles. However, a physical BC registered office and records office is mandatory. The bank may also request an in-person visit for the authorized signatory if enhanced due diligence flags unusual ownership structures or non-resident controllers; this discretion is exercised on a case-by-case basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) treated as a pass-through or hybrid entity for foreign tax purposes, causing ambiguity in beneficial ownership and economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a legal opinion from a Canadian corporate law firm confirming the ULC's valid incorporation under BC law and its unlimited liability attributes; produce the Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, Memorandum of Articles, corporate registers, and a detailed ownership chart showing ultimate beneficial owners. Submit CRA business number registration, GST/HST account confirmation, and, if applicable, a section 2602 election or tax treatment memorandum for the ULC's Canadian federal tax status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of low-value recurring revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, which may be flagged as suspicious for unregulated digital content sales.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed platform agreements with Apple and Google, monthly payment settlement reports, bank statements of the acquiring relationships, and a compliance narrative tying each transaction to a user subscription. Implement and evidence an AML/ATF program including customer identification thresholds, transaction monitoring, and FINTRAC registration if applicable. Include a data flow diagram showing app store clearing to the Canadian bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border outbound remittances to non-resident authors or content licensors in high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a complete roster of authors and licensors with contractual agreements, copyright assignments, and tax forms (NR4, NR301, or W-8BEN-E). Apply enhanced due diligence for payees in sanctioned or high-risk countries; perform OFAC / Government of Canada sanctions screening; retain ITR (International Transfer Report) records for FINTRAC; use a payment aggregator with KYB/KYC vetting for each payee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from foreign directors or shareholders into a BC ULC may be scrutinized for money-laundering, particularly if funds originate offshore.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a share subscription agreement, director resolutions approving the issuance, bank reference letters for the remitting institution, and a source-of-wealth statement from the subscriber. Use a designated Capital Escrow Account with a clear memo 'Share Subscription – CA_ULC', and complete the bank's beneficial ownership and politically exposed persons (PEP) questionnaires. Retain a legal opinion on the application of Canada's anti-money laundering rules to the inbound equity transfer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital to the BC ULC must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire/CHIPS for USD) to the Capital Escrow Account held with a Tier 1 Canadian bank. The payment instruction must reference the company legal name, the ULC registration number, and the memo 'ULC Share Subscription – [Investor Ref]'. Use the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' for equity injection, or 'BOND' if structured as intercompany debt. For amounts exceeding CAD 10,000, the bank will trigger FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting; it is prudent to submit a Notification of Payment Tracker (if applicable) and provide the bank with a ready evidence pack including: incorporation documents, share subscription agreement, board resolution, and source-of-funds declaration. No regulatory pre-approval is needed; however, the bank's compliance team must clear the injection before funds are made operational.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound author royalty and license payments should use SWIFT MT103 for non-Canadian beneficiaries, with standard 56A/D/57A beneficiary bank information and purpose code 'ROYL' (royalty) or 'GDSV' (digital service) as appropriate. For Canadian payees, use Payment Canada's EFT (Credit Clearing System) or Real-Time Rail (RTR, if available) with ISO 20022 messages. For high-volume serialized webnovel author payouts, an integrated mass-pay platform (e.g., through Wise, Airwallex, or a FINTRAC-registered PSP) can batch MT103/102 messages, but core operating cash positions must remain in the Canadian bank account to facilitate FX settlements. A Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) is generally not required because the business involves digital content licences; if an LC is demanded for platform exclusivity agreements, a stand-by LC may be issued by the Tier 1 bank against cash collateral. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlements are received through the relevant payment gateway into an ordinary corporate account after card network clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (up to 12 months) with a Canadian Schedule I bank for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/CNH hedges

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) available at major Canadian bank counterparties for currencies not deliverable in the Canadian market, generally sourced from the offshore non-deliverable market (e.g., CNH, KRW)
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement for medium-term balance sheet hedging of foreign-currency receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies / BC Registries and Online Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty applies; if two consecutive annual report periods are missed, the Registrar may administratively dissolve the company after notice, ending corporate existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Transparency Register Annual Significant Individual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (confirmation embedded in BC Annual Report); transparency register kept at BC records office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same BC Annual Report deadline as above; register entries updated within the prescribed record time after any change in significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under BCBCA for failure to maintain or update the register; directors and officers may be subject to personal fines; failure does not cure annual report default and may contribute to administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after taxation year-end; any balance of tax payable is due by the general remittance due date, usually 2 months or 3 months after year-end for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated-failure penalty of 10%; CRA may assess tax arbitrarily and issue a requirement to file.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset, or employee size threshold applies under BCBCA. An independent auditor is mandatory unless shareholders validly resolve to dispense with an auditor for a non-reporting company; reporting issuers cannot waive, and a shareholder demand or Registrar direction can make the audit compulsory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in CPA Canada Handbook Part I for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) may be used by a private non-reporting ULC; financial statements must support statutory income tax reporting to the CRA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A BC private unlimited liability company must maintain a transparency register of individuals with significant control, defined as holders of 25% or more of shares or voting rights or persons with de facto control. On any shareholding transfer, the register must be updated within the prescribed period, and the annual report filing must confirm that the transparency register has been maintained and updated. The register is not publicly filed but must be produced to the regulator on demand.

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined (15% federal + 12% BC) for general business income; 11% combined (9% federal + 2% BC) for first CAD 500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (not available to a ULC controlled by non-residents).
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No federal/BC income tax holiday; SR&ED investment tax credits (35%/15%); BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit 17.5% on qualifying labour expenditures if the platform constitutes interactive digital media; ULC is not eligible for small business deduction if controlled by non-residents.
